23 to 31 inches, very pale brown (10YR 7/3) loam, yellowish brown (10YR 5/4) moist; massive; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; strongly effervescent; a few medium mottles of segregated lime; 10 percent of volume in limestone pebbles; gradual wavy boundary.
31 to 43 inches, pink (7.5YR 7/3) gravelly loam, light brown (7.5YR 6/4) moist; massive structure; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; strongly effervescent; 30 percent of volume is limestone gravel; clear irregular boundary.
C5 43 to 50 inches, very gravelly loam containing 60 percent limestone gravels.
The surface layer includes textures of loam and gravelly loam. Depth to the calcareous soil is 2 to 8 inches. The Cca contains 15 to 35 percent calcium carbonate equivalent. Coarse fragments in the 10 to 40 inch section range from 0 to 35 percent. The soil color hues are 7.5YR through 2.5Y. The chroma is 2 to 3. A horizon color range is grayish brown and brown. The Cca horizon color range is light brown, light gray and pale yellow. In some areas the soils have loamy gravel at depths below 40 inches. Lime occurs as flour, soft masses, and lime crusts on the coarse fragments.
Harvey soils are associated with Stormitt, Colby, Clapper, and Toluca soils. They contain fewer coarse fragments than the Stormitt and Clapper soils. They are more limy than the Colby soils, an they lack the thin B2t horizon of the Toluca soils.
Harvey loam, rolling (8 to 15 percent slopes) (Hcc).
This soil is on eroded parts of benches and fans along river and intermittent stream valleys. The areas are usually small and often are separated by narrow drainageways filled with deep alluvial material. Local relief is 20 to 30 feet. Slopes are 6 to 7 percent on the wide ridges between shallow drainageways. Slopes of 10 to 15 percent occur in areas where deep drainageways separate narrow ridges. The slope length is 75 to 200 feet. The soil has a profile similar to the typical one described for the series. Mapped with this soil are spots of the gravelly loam type in the series, Colby silty clay loam and Clapper gravelly loam. The gravelly loam Harvey soil occurs along the sharp breaks to the deep drainageways or on narrow ridges. The Clapper soils occupy a narrow band along the rim of major drainageways or on sharp breaks on the land surface.
Runoff is moderate and the erosion hazard is severe.
This soil is used for range. A few small areas are in dry cropland.
(Capability Unit IVe-3 Dryland; Silty range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 3L).
